config.notes: Lincoln University (NZ). Course pages are www.lincoln.ac.nz/study/study-programmes/programme-search/<slug>/ (server-rendered, no page JSON). Key-facts panel under the H1: "Upcoming start dates Semester 1 - 22 Feb 2027 Semester 2 - 19 Jul 2027 [or November Summer School - 09 Nov 2026] Qualification <level> Duration <n> years full-time Credits <n> Location <campus> Fee estimate 2027 Domestic: $x (N credits) International: $y (N credits)". The bracketed credits are the load the amount covers: fee is read only when quoted per 120 credits (one full-time year, NZD). Amounts quoted for 60, 180 or 240 credits (certificates, 1.5- and 2-year taught masters) are partial-year or whole-programme totals and are deliberately not read. Term mapping Semester 1 = February, Semester 2 = July is from the course pages themselves ("Semester 1 (late February) Semester 2 (early July)"). IELTS is not on course pages (they link to the central English language requirements page). No course code printed on pages. Delivery (mode) is read from the key-facts Location line ("Lincoln University Campus", "Lincoln University Campus or Online", "Online"), which applies to international students too; the old mode pattern read study load (full-time) and was replaced. International view (5 Oct 13:02): the course page prints the domestic and international fee side by side for every visitor (no student-type switch or URL variant needed). course_title_strip removes the catalogue's "(Level n)" so pages rebound by hand are confirmed by their heading. Entry requirement (Platform Admin 15:36): the "Entry requirements <text>" panel up to the first full stop or the overseas/English note (max 200 characters), shown for review only. Fee from a whole-programme fee (Platform Admin 15:34): where the international amount is quoted for 180, 240, 360 or 480 credits (the whole programme, e.g. "International: $74,000 (240 credits)") fee_total takes it and course_years the full-time years ("Duration 2 years full-time"); the worker records annual = total / years. 60-credit (half-year) amounts are not read. Exit awards: none printed on stored pages.
